sentences.en: were originally composed in Latin as the basis of a formal public disputation or debate at the university, but they were soon translated into German and put into print,
sentences.zh: 最初是用拉丁文撰写的，作为大学里正式公开辩论的基础，但它们很快被翻译成德文并付诸印刷，

sentences.zh: 不，我不认为此时他有什么特别之处能让人觉得他与众不同。

sentences.en: And again, what makes it all the more improbable is that I think that there is a sense, particularly
sentences.zh: 再说一遍，这也是最不可思议的地方，因为我觉得有一种感觉，尤其是

sentences.en: if you grow up, I think, in a kind of culturally Protestant country like Britain, you assume
sentences.zh: 如果你是在像英国这样文化上属于新教的国家长大的，你就会认为

sentences.en: that it's just waiting for someone like Luther to come along and poke at the rotten oak of the medieval church, and it will all just collapse.
sentences.zh: 这一切都只是在等待像路德这样的人出现，去敲击中世纪教会那根腐朽的顶梁柱，然后它就会轰然倒塌。

sentences.en: Fat monks, corruption, people having feasts while the peasants are starving, fake relics.
sentences.zh: 肥胖的修士、腐败、农民在挨饿而权贵们在大吃大喝、虚假的圣物。

sentences.en: Tom, I hate to tell you, but I think for about the first 30 years of my life, that's pretty much what I thought.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，我很遗憾地告诉你，我想在我人生大约前三十年里，我基本上就是这么认为的。

sentences.en: I mean, I kind of still deep down think was the story with the Catholic church, but you are now going to tell me that's not right at all.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，我内心深处某种程度上依然觉得这就是天主教教会的故事，但你现在要告诉我，这完全不是那么回事。

sentences.en: Well, so I think that assumption is hardwired into the very phrase, the Reformation, with a capital R.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以我觉得这种假设已经深深烙印在“宗教改革”（The Reformation）这个词本身里了，首字母还是大写的。

sentences.en: Because, of course, that's a very, very Protestant perspective.
sentences.zh: 因为，当然，这是一个非常非常新教的视角。

sentences.en: And in fact, right the way up until the end of the 19th century, it's only Protestants who ever use it.
sentences.zh: 事实上，一直到19世纪末，也只有新教徒在使用这个词。

sentences.en: Because I think Catholics would point out that Reformation, which comes from the Latin word reformatio, remaking, is actually, it's not specific to Protestantism.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为天主教会会指出，“宗教改革”（Reformation）这个词源于拉丁语 reformatio，即重塑，实际上它并非新教所独有。

sentences.en: It is something that has been continuous throughout the entire history of the church.
sentences.zh: 这是贯穿整个教会历史的一项连续不断的进程。

sentences.en: And the truth is that the medieval church that the Protestant Reformation overthrows is itself the product of a reformatio, is itself a kind of revolutionary institution.
sentences.zh: 事实是，被新教宗教改革推翻的中世纪教会本身就是 reformatio 的产物，其本身就是一种革命性的机构。

sentences.en: Because the first Reformation, and this is important background to understand what Luther
sentences.zh: 因为第一次宗教改革——这是理解路德所作所为的重要背景——

sentences.en: is about, because the first Reformation happens not in the 16th century, but in the 11th century.
sentences.zh: 因为第一次宗教改革不是发生在16世纪，而是发生在11世纪。

sentences.en: And it matters because the second Reformation is, you know, it's a reaction to it, but it's also bred of it.
sentences.zh: 这之所以重要，是因为第二次宗教改革既是对它的反弹，也是孕育自它。

sentences.en: So I think we should just give a portrait of this Reformation, because it is what Luther is going to be reacting againSt.
sentences.zh: 所以我觉得我们应该先描绘一下这场宗教改革的肖像，因为这正是路德将要反抗的对象。

sentences.en: So the key features of this revolutionary institution that is the medieval church.
sentences.zh: 那么，这个作为中世纪教会的革命性机构有哪些关键特征呢？

sentences.en: It divides the world into two, in a way that had never happened before in any kind of culture in the world.
sentences.zh: 它将世界一分为二，这是世界上任何其他文化中从未有过的方式。

sentences.en: You have a dimension of the cyclum, which is the kind of the earthly mortal dimension, and will give us the word secular.
sentences.zh: 你拥有世俗界（saeculum）的维度，也就是世俗凡人的维度，这也是我们今天“世俗”（secular）一词的来源。

sentences.en: And then you have the dimension of the church, which is radiant and pure and constitutes the link or the religio in Latin to heaven.
sentences.zh: 然后你拥有教会的维度，它是光辉而纯洁的，构成了人间与天堂之间的纽带（在拉丁语中称为 religio）。

sentences.en: So there you have kind of what will become the key dividing line, which we still have to this day between the secular and the religious.
sentences.zh: 所以，在这里你看到了将成为关键分界线的东西，这条分界线至今仍然存在于世俗与宗教之间。

sentences.en: And the clergy who are called the religiosi, these are the people who guard the dimension of the religio, the bond joining humans to heaven.
sentences.zh: 而被称为“隐修人员”（religiosi）的神职人员，正是守护 religio 维度的人，守护着连接人类与天堂的纽带。

sentences.en: So these are, dare I say, professional Christians, which is quite unusual anywhere in the world to have a class who take up, in some places, a 10% of the population.
sentences.zh: 所以，这些可以说是职业基督徒，这在世界上任何地方都是相当罕见的，竟然有一个阶层在某些地方占据了人口的10%。

sentences.en: So their job is just to be Christians.
sentences.zh: 所以他们的工作就是做基督徒。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And they are marked by chastity, which again is very distinctive and which really only is introduced in the 11th century.
sentences.zh: 他们以贞洁为标志，这也是非常独特的，而且实际上直到11世纪才被引入。

sentences.en: And by their use of Latin, which is again, a kind of marker of the fact that they belong to a universal, timeless church.
sentences.zh: 并且通过他们对拉丁语的使用，这同样标志着他们属于一个普遍的、超越时间的教会。

sentences.en: They have a very complex hierarchy, obviously with the Pope at the head of it.
sentences.zh: 他们拥有非常复杂的等级制度，显而易见，教皇是最高首领。

sentences.en: And beneath him, there are all kinds of different clergy.
sentences.zh: 在他之下，有着各种各样不同的神职人员。

sentences.en: So there are what are called secular clergy, clergy who are operating out in the dimension of the cyclum with the laity.
sentences.zh: 有被称为世俗神职人员的群体，他们在世俗界（saeculum）中与平信徒一同活动。

sentences.en: These are like your friars and whatnot.
sentences.zh: 这些就像是你的修道士之类的人。

sentences.en: So these are the archbishops, the bishops, right the way down to the parish priests, the friars, the monks, the nuns, these are called regular clergy.
sentences.zh: 这些是大主教、主教，一直到本堂神父、修士、修道士、修女，这些被称为正规神职人员。

sentences.en: So these are people who are taking the kind of the narrow path to heaven, but the surest path to heaven.
sentences.zh: 所以这些人走的是通往天堂的狭窄道路，但却是最确定的通往天堂之路。

sentences.en: And they, in a way, are kind of storing up kind of benefits for the vast mass of the
sentences.zh: 某种程度上，他们一直在为广大普通

sentences.en: Christian people.
sentences.zh: 基督徒积累功德。

sentences.en: Because like all revolutionary institutions, the church gets its validity from offering people the promise of a better life.
sentences.zh: 因为就像所有革命性机构一样，教会的合法性来自于向人们承诺更好的生活。

sentences.en: So you have justice on this world, in the mortal world, and this justice is provided for people
sentences.zh: 所以在尘世间、在凡人世界里，你拥有正义，而这种正义之所以能够提供给人们，

sentences.en: as a result of a kind of entire framework of law that derives from the church fathers, from church councils, from decrees of the popes.
sentences.zh: 是因为有一整套源自教会神父、教会会议以及教皇法令的法律框架。

sentences.en: And these are collectively known as canons.
sentences.zh: 这些统称为法规（canons）。

sentences.en: So the framework of church law is called the canon law.
sentences.zh: 所以教会法律的框架被称为教会法（canon law）。

sentences.en: And this is seen as expressive of God's justice.
sentences.zh: 这被视为上帝正义的表达。

sentences.en: And there's always a tension, isn't there, between that, the canon law, and the separate hierarchy that the church has, and its own practices, its institutions, and all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 这里总是存在一种紧张关系，不是吗？在教会法与教会拥有的独立等级制度、它自身的实践、机构以及诸如此类的事情之间。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: There's always a tension between that and like the local king, Henry II, Henry VIII, whoever, who thinks they're kind of invading my privileges.
sentences.zh: 在这一点与地方国王（比如亨利二世、亨利八世或其他人，他们认为这些侵犯了自己的特权）之间，总是存在着紧张关系。

sentences.en: And, you know, that doesn't start with Henry VIII wanting a son.
sentences.zh: 而且，你知道，这并不是从亨利八世想要个儿子开始的。

sentences.en: No, no, it doesn't.
sentences.zh: 不，不，并不是。

sentences.en: That's been there for centuries.
sentences.zh: 这种现象已经存在了几个世纪。

sentences.en: Canon law begins to be constructed in the 12th century.
sentences.zh: 教会法在12世纪开始成型。

sentences.en: And by the 16th century, by the time of Luther, it's this vast edifice.
sentences.zh: 到16世纪路德的时代，它已经成为一座庞大的建筑。

sentences.en: As also is the edifice of the spiritual economy that the church is presiding over.
sentences.zh: 教会所主导的精神经济大厦也是如此。

sentences.en: Because, of course, what it ultimately is promising is the promise of heaven, of salvation.
sentences.zh: 因为，当然，它最终承诺的是天堂的承诺，是救赎。

sentences.en: But what will prevent you from getting to heaven is sin.
sentences.zh: 但阻止你进入天堂的是罪过。

sentences.en: And sin, you know, if you're not going to go to hell, you have to pay it down.
sentences.zh: 而罪过，你知道的，如果你不想下地狱，你就必须把它清偿掉。

sentences.en: You have to get rid of it.
sentences.zh: 你必须摆脱它。

sentences.en: And this is where indulgences come in.
sentences.zh: 这就是赎罪券发挥作用的地方。

sentences.en: So, indulgences, they can wipe your sin completely clean.
sentences.zh: 所以，赎罪券可以彻底抹去你的罪孽。

sentences.en: But, Tom, you're not going to hell straight away, are you?
sentences.zh: 但是，汤姆，你不会马上就下地狱吧？

sentences.en: Well, so, effectively, if you were sinless in this life, which is almost impossible, so even saints, you might go straight to heaven.
sentences.zh: 嗯，所以实际上，如果你在这生中毫无罪过——这几乎是不可能的，所以即使是圣人，你也许会直接上天堂。

sentences.en: But the vast mass of people are going to have to work off their debt of sin in a place called purgatory.
sentences.zh: 但绝大多数人将不得不在一个叫做炼狱的地方偿还他们的罪债。

sentences.en: So, that's like a waiting room.
sentences.zh: 所以，那就好像是一个候诊室。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: You're not, it's not hell.
sentences.zh: 你不是……那不是地狱。

sentences.en: A waiting room with fire.
sentences.zh: 一个带火的候诊室。

sentences.en: So, it's like a lesser hell?
sentences.zh: 所以，这就像是一个低配版的地狱？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's like hell with a time limit.
sentences.zh: 这就像是有时间限制的地狱。

sentences.en: So, you've been, you know, a terrible man.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可能是一个，你知道的，极其糟糕的人。

sentences.en: You're Himmler.
sentences.zh: 你是希姆莱。

sentences.en: You're going to hell.
sentences.zh: 你要下地狱。

sentences.en: You're just a common or garden offender like you and I.
sentences.zh: 而你只是个你我一样的泛泛之辈、普通罪人。

sentences.en: You know, we're ordinary sinful people.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们都是普通的有罪之人。

sentences.en: We might go to purgatory for a thousand years.
sentences.zh: 我们可能会在炼狱里待上一千年。

sentences.en: You know, who knows?
sentences.zh: 你知道，谁知道呢？

sentences.en: I think in your case, Dominic, it's slightly longer.
sentences.zh: 我想对你而言，多米尼克，时间可能会稍微长一点。

sentences.en: Thanks.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: It could bear with Himmler.
sentences.zh: 这或许能跟希姆莱有得一拼。

sentences.en: But you could work this down.
sentences.zh: 但你可以通过修行来减少这个时间。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So, you could make prayers to the saints and the virgin who will intervene with God.
sentences.zh: 所以，你可以向圣徒和圣母祈祷，他们会为你向上帝求情。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Or you could, you know, charitable donations, good works.
sentences.zh: 或者你可以，你知道的，进行慈善捐赠、行善积德。

sentences.en: You could go on a pilgrimage.
sentences.zh: 你可以去朝圣。

sentences.en: And above all, there are masses.
sentences.zh: 最重要的是，还有弥撒。

sentences.en: And the mass, it's the celebration of the sacrifice of Christ on the cross.
sentences.zh: 弥撒，它是对基督在十字架上牺牲的庆祝。

sentences.en: And it's made vivid and real in the bread and wine.
sentences.zh: 它在面包和酒中变得生动而真实。

sentences.en: Christ is literally present there.
sentences.zh: 基督字面意义上就实实在在地临在于那里。

sentences.en: And this is a way for the Christian people to kind of experience a sense of common identity and to commune with the mystery of their faith.
sentences.zh: 这是基督徒体验共同身份认同感以及与他们信仰的奥秘进行共融的一种方式。

sentences.en: So, this is why churches are set aside as sacred places.
sentences.zh: 所以，这就是为什么教堂被划为神圣场所。

sentences.en: So, you have images, you have icons, you have incense, you have all the kind of stuff that
sentences.zh: 因此，你有圣像、圣图、香，还有所有这些……

sentences.en: I'm sure would rouse your Protestant suspicions.
sentences.zh: 我确信这些会激起你作为新教徒的疑心。

sentences.en: I actually like icons, Tom.
sentences.zh: 我其实挺喜欢圣像的，汤姆。

sentences.en: I love an icon.
sentences.zh: 我可太喜欢圣像了。

sentences.en: Good, good.
sentences.zh: 很好，很好。

sentences.en: I love the kind of the Orthodox Church.
sentences.zh: 我喜欢那种东正教会。

sentences.en: Big fan of the Orthodox Church.
sentences.zh: 东正教会的超级粉丝。

sentences.en: But the role that masses play in the spiritual economy is that they are kind of believed to transcend place and time.
sentences.zh: 但弥撒在精神经济中所扮演的角色在于，人们相信它们能够超越空间和时间。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And to link all Christians to, you know, the sacrifice of Christ on the cross.
sentences.zh: 并将所有基督徒与基督在十字架上的牺牲联系起来。

sentences.en: And therefore, they have an incredible efficacy in burning away the sins of the dead in purgatory.
sentences.zh: 因此，它们在焚烧炼狱中死者罪孽方面具有不可思议的功效。

sentences.en: And so, by the 15th century, the idea of wealthy people paying monks or whoever to perform masses for the dead has become a crucial part of Christian piety.
sentences.zh: 因此，到了15世纪，富有的人花钱请修道士或其他什么人为死者做弥撒的想法，已经成为基督教虔诚的重要组成部分。

sentences.en: So, Tom, two points about masses.
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，关于弥撒有两点。

sentences.en: So, one is, in a weird way, actually, I never thought I'd say this to you on this of all subjects.
sentences.zh: 第一点是，说实话，以一种奇怪的方式，我从没想过会在这样一个话题上对你这么说。

sentences.en: I think you're almost slightly underselling what a massive deal, literally a massive deal, the mass is.
sentences.zh: 我觉得你简直有点低估了弥撒是多么重大的一件事，字面意义上的重大事件。

sentences.en: Because most people would only go and take communion once a year.
sentences.zh: 因为大多数人一年只会去领一次圣餐。

sentences.en: Is that right?
sentences.zh: 是这样吗？

sentences.en: And they would get the bread, but not the wine.
sentences.zh: 而且他们只能分到面包，分不到酒。

sentences.en: The wine is reserved for the prieSt.
sentences.zh: 酒是留给神父的。

sentences.en: But this is a moment of extraordinary power in your life, right?
sentences.zh: 但这是你一生中具有非凡力量的时刻，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's almost as though you were approaching the heart of a nuclear reactor or something.
sentences.zh: 这几乎就像是你正在接近核反应堆的核心或者类似的地方。

sentences.en: The mass is the reactor that is powering everything.
sentences.zh: 弥撒就是为一切提供动力的反应堆。

sentences.en: And it's so potent that only priests can approach it.
sentences.zh: 而且它威力如此巨大，以至于只有神父才能靠近它。

sentences.en: And even then, only with extreme care.
sentences.zh: 即便如此，也必须极其小心翼翼。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And for the laity, you know, it's too dangerous to approach.
sentences.zh: 而对于平信徒来说，你知道的，靠近它太危险了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: It's the bit of the Raiders of the Lost Ark when they take the lid off the Ark of the Covenant and all the stuff is flying out.
sentences.zh: 就像《夺宝奇兵》里的那个桥段，他们打开约柜的盖子，所有的东西都飞了出来。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That's the moment in your life, isn't it?
sentences.zh: 那正是你生命中的那个时刻，不是吗？

sentences.en: Where, I mean, God is literally there.
sentences.zh: 上帝就在那里，字面意义上的在那里。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Literally there.
sentences.zh: 字面意义上的在那里。

sentences.en: Literally in the bread and wine.
sentences.zh: 字面意义上就在面包和酒里。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: The bread and the wine are the body and blood.
sentences.zh: 面包和酒就是圣体和圣血。

sentences.en: But, I mean, God is literally present.
sentences.zh: 但是，我的意思是，上帝确实实实在在地临在于此。

sentences.en: But also, the other thing I was going to say, that thing about saying masses for the dead to get you out of purgatory.
sentences.zh: 不过还有一件事我要说，就是为死者做弥撒以助其脱离炼狱的那件事。

sentences.en: But am I not right in saying that that industry, because it is an industry, is more developed in Germany than in any other part of Christendom?
sentences.zh: 我没说错吧，那种产业——因为它确实是一个产业——在德国的发展程度比基督教世界的任何其他地方都要高？

sentences.en: So, somebody like Luther growing up, it looms, again, massively large in a way that it wouldn't
sentences.zh: 所以像路德这样的人在成长过程中，这件事再次占据了极其巨大的分量，如果他在意大利、西班牙或其他弥撒产业没那么发达的地方，就不会有这种感觉。

sentences.en: if he was in Italy or Spain or somewhere, where the mass industry is not quite as developed.
sentences.zh: 如果他在意大利、西班牙或其他弥撒产业没那么发达的地方，就不会有这种感觉。

sentences.en: So, that explains why he ends up kicking against it and why it becomes so incredibly controversial in Germany and Switzerland and the kind of Baltic and Scandinavia and so on.
sentences.zh: 这就解释了为什么他最终会起来反抗它，以及为什么它在德国、瑞士、波罗的海和斯堪的纳维亚等地变得如此极具争议。

sentences.en: But again, I mean, it takes some time to take the dramatic step of kicking against it.
sentences.zh: 但话说回来，采取反抗它的戏剧性一步确实需要一些时间。

sentences.en: Because I think to begin with that, you know, he's a schoolboy or he's a student, he's not really thinking about it.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为一开始，你知道的，他还是个学童或学生，并没有真正去考虑这些。

sentences.en: Because for most people who are not kind of professional Christians in McCulloch's formulation,
sentences.zh: 因为对于大多数并非麦卡洛克所说的“职业基督徒”的人来说，

sentences.en: this is, it's not something you necessarily believe in, in the way that we believe or don't believe in things.
sentences.zh: 这并不是那种你必然会去信仰的东西，不像我们现在这样去相信或不相信某些事情。

sentences.en: Because this is part of the course of modernity that Luther is going to set Europe on.
sentences.zh: 因为这是路德将把欧洲带入的现代性历程的一部分。

sentences.en: So, I think for most people, it's just kind of part of the air that they breathe in.
sentences.zh: 所以，我认为对大多数人来说，这就像是他们呼吸的空气的一部分。

sentences.en: And I think it's one of the aspects of the pre-Reformation culture that is hardest for us to get our heads around.
sentences.zh: 我认为这也是前宗教改革文化中最难让我们理解的方面之一。

sentences.en: Because I think that the way that the Reformation changes our relationship to belief is one of the profoundest aspects of what makes it revolutionary.
sentences.zh: 因为我认为宗教改革改变我们与信仰关系的方式，正是其具有革命性最深刻的体现之一。

sentences.en: So, for us, what do you believe in or what don't you believe in?
sentences.zh: 所以对我们来说，你信仰什么或者你不信仰什么？

sentences.en: It's a crucial marker of our identity.
sentences.zh: 这是我们身份认同的一个关键标志。

sentences.en: But it's really, I think, different, say, in 15th century Latin Christendom.
sentences.zh: 但我认为，这与15世纪的拉丁基督教世界大不相同。

sentences.en: So, say, when Christians call Jews or Muslims unbelievers, they're not really defining them in terms of the fact that what Jews or Muslims believe is wrong.
sentences.zh: 所以，当基督徒称犹太人或穆斯林为异教徒时，他们并不是在根据犹太人或穆斯林的信仰是错误的来定义他们。

sentences.en: It's just that they don't believe in the stuff that everyone in Latin Europe is taking for granted.
sentences.zh: 只是他们不相信拉丁欧洲每个人都视为理所当然的事情。

sentences.en: So, Tom, I loved this section in your notes.
sentences.zh: 所以，汤姆，我太喜欢你笔记里的这一部分了。

sentences.en: Because it really, I mean, sometimes I'm very hard on you and the rest is history.
sentences.zh: 因为确实，有时候我对你要求很严格，而剩下的就是历史了。

sentences.en: But I think here, I just thought, wow, this is so interesting.
sentences.zh: 但在这里我觉得，哇，这太有趣了。

sentences.en: Because, like many people, you know, I'd often thought, did people really believe this?
sentences.zh: 因为就像许多人一样，你知道的，我经常想，人们真的相信这个吗？

sentences.en: Did they really believe that the body and blood turned into all that stuff?
sentences.zh: 他们真的相信圣体和圣血会变成那些东西吗？

sentences.en: You know, relics, indulgences.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，圣物、赎罪券。

sentences.en: How could they believe it?
sentences.zh: 他们怎么能相信呢？

sentences.en: But I think what you're bringing out here is that in a way they don't really think about it.
sentences.zh: 但我认为你在这里揭示的是，在某种程度上他们根本不去想它。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 不。

sentences.en: Because why would you?
sentences.zh: 因为你为什么要多想呢？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: It's like you and I know, for example, that human beings need oxygen to survive.
sentences.zh: 就像你和我都清楚，举例来说，人类需要氧气才能生存。

sentences.en: Or that the universe was born in the Big Bang.
sentences.zh: 或者说宇宙诞生于宇宙大爆炸。

sentences.en: But we only know that because everyone we know thinks it.
sentences.zh: 但我们之所以知道这一点，纯粹是因为我们认识的所有人都这么认为。

sentences.en: We've been told it.
sentences.zh: 我们一直被灌输这种观念。

sentences.en: And we take it on truSt.
sentences.zh: 而我们对此深信不疑。

sentences.en: And we just take it completely for granted.
sentences.zh: 并且我们将其视为理所当然。

sentences.en: And that's how they thought about the devil, indulgences, purgatory, all that stuff.
sentences.zh: 他们对魔鬼、赎罪券、炼狱以及诸如此类的事物的看法也是如此。

sentences.en: They didn't sit up late at night debating whether or not it was true.
sentences.zh: 他们可不会深夜坐在一起辩论这到底是真是假。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Because it obviously was true to them.
sentences.zh: 因为对他们来说，这显然是真的。

sentences.en: Well, I think a kind of a really fascinating parallel would be with, say, people's attitudes to epidemiology during the COVID lockdowns.
sentences.zh: 嗯，我觉得一个非常迷人的类比，比如，人们在新冠封锁期间对流行病学的态度。

sentences.en: That most people accepted what they were told by the epidemiologists.
sentences.zh: 大多数人都接受了流行病学家告诉他们的话。

sentences.en: Because why wouldn't they?
sentences.zh: 因为他们为什么不呢？

sentences.en: It's the epidemiologists who know.
sentences.zh: 是流行病学家才懂这些。

sentences.en: And so the theologians are the kind of the medieval equivalent of epidemiologists.
sentences.zh: 所以神学家就相当于中世纪的流行病学家。

sentences.en: And you may wonder, well, you know, how do they know?
sentences.zh: 你可能会想，嗯，你知道，他们是怎么知道的？

sentences.en: How do they get their certainty?
sentences.zh: 他们是如何确信这一切的？

sentences.en: And they get it because they have revelation in the form of scripture.
sentences.zh: 他们之所以确信，是因为他们有圣经形式的神圣启示。

sentences.en: But also they have what is called by intellectuals in the universities, scientia, so science.
sentences.zh: 但他们也拥有大学知识分子所说的scientia，也就是科学。

sentences.en: But it's not science in our sense.
sentences.zh: 但这不是我们理解的那种科学。

sentences.en: It's the knowledge that can be deduced from revelation via kind of deduction, via rigorous study.
sentences.zh: 它是通过演绎、通过严格的研究，从启示中推导出来的知识。

sentences.en: And so this is how purgatory comes to be deduced.
sentences.zh: 炼狱就是这样被推导出来的。

sentences.en: Purgatory is not mentioned in scripture, but you can deduce it from kind of various conclusions that can be drawn from scripture.
sentences.zh: 圣经中没有提到炼狱，但你可以从圣经中得出各种结论来推导它。

sentences.en: And so the whole edifice of, you know, this this kind of framework of belief is like a kind of enormous cathedral that you don't have to go into the cathedral to be aware of it.
sentences.zh: 所以整个庞大的建筑，你知道的，这种信仰框架就像是一座巨大的大教堂，你甚至不需要走进这座大教堂就能感受到它的存在。

sentences.en: It is looming up over you.
sentences.zh: 它就高高耸立在你的头顶。

sentences.en: You know, because they're the experts.
sentences.zh: 你知道，因为他们是专家。

sentences.en: Exactly.
sentences.zh: 确实如此。

sentences.en: And only a madman.
sentences.zh: 只有疯子才会……

sentences.en: You know, in 2024, somebody who said, well, I don't believe the world is round, actually.
sentences.zh: 你知道，在2024年，如果有人说，嗯，其实我不相信地球是圆的。

sentences.en: You know, you would be like, it's just eccentric for the sake of it.
sentences.zh: 你知道，你会觉得这纯粹是为了标新立异而标新立异。

sentences.en: What's the point in going against what everybody knows to be true?
sentences.zh: 去违背人所共知的事实，有什么意义呢？

sentences.en: Well, let's pursue that COVID analogy.
sentences.zh: 好吧，让我们顺着这个新冠的类比继续探讨。

sentences.en: Of course, during COVID, there are skeptics.
sentences.zh: 当然，在新冠期间，也是有怀疑论者的。

sentences.en: I mean, there are people who kick back against what the medical establishment are telling them.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，有些人对医疗体制告诉他们的东西进行反击。

sentences.en: And so likewise in the Middle Ages, of course, you do have people who are kicking back against what the church authorities are telling them.
sentences.zh: 同样，在中世纪，当然也有人对教会权威告诉他们的东西进行反击。

sentences.en: And these are people who, of course, are called heretics.
sentences.zh: 这些人，毫无疑问，被称为异端。

sentences.en: And if they're inveterate as heretics and they refuse to recant, then they're burned.
sentences.zh: 如果他们执迷不悟且拒绝悔改，就会被烧死。

sentences.en: And in the 15th century, there is quite a vivid consciousness of this tradition.
sentences.zh: 到了15世纪，人们对这种传统有着相当生动的认知。

sentences.en: Because there have been lots of heretics.
sentences.zh: 因为曾经有过很多异端。

sentences.en: I mean, there's been a guy called Peter Valdo in France, very famously, Tom, dear to my heart, the former master of Balliol, John Wycliffe.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，法国有个叫皮埃尔·瓦尔多的人，非常著名；汤姆，我亲爱的前贝利奥尔学院院长约翰·威克里夫。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: And in the 1490s, there's a guy called Savonarola in Florence, who's a sort of becomes the leader of the city.
sentences.zh: 在1490年代，佛罗伦萨有个叫萨沃纳罗拉的人，他成为了这座城市的某种领袖。

sentences.en: But the guy you're going to be talking about is the real precursor to Luther.
sentences.zh: 但你要谈论的那个人才是路德真正的先驱。

sentences.en: That's Jan Hus, right?
sentences.zh: 那是扬·胡斯，对吧？

sentences.en: So Jan Hus, he is from Prague.
sentences.zh: 所以扬·胡斯来自布拉格。

sentences.en: He's a scholar there at the university, immensely charismatic, intellectually brilliant, huge personal integrity, very influenced by Wycliffe.
sentences.zh: 他是那里的大学学者，极具个人魅力，才华横溢，拥有崇高的人格，深受威克里夫的影响。

sentences.en: And Wycliffe is questioning the authority of the papacy, questioning all kinds of aspects of church teaching.
sentences.zh: 威克里夫对教皇的权威提出质疑，对教会教义的各个方面提出质疑。

sentences.en: Hus is influenced by him.
sentences.zh: 胡斯受到了他的影响。

sentences.en: And so Hus, following Wycliffe's example, is teaching that the Bible is the ultimate source
sentences.zh: 因此，胡斯效仿威克里夫的榜样，教导人们圣经才是最终的权威来源

sentences.en: of authority and that the traditions of the church are kind of irrelevant compared to the sanctity of the Bible.
sentences.zh: 并认为与圣经的神圣性相比，教会的传统根本不值一提。

sentences.en: That the clergy are so corrupt that maybe the entire fabric of the church is corrupt.
sentences.zh: 他认为神职人员如此腐败，以至于整个教会的结构可能都已经腐败了。

sentences.en: And again, he is scorning the claim of the papacy to have a primacy that's been given by God.
sentences.zh: 而且，他又一次对教皇拥有上帝赋予的至高无上权力这一主张表示不屑。

sentences.en: And aren't there two other things that are interesting about Hus?
sentences.zh: 关于胡斯，还有另外两件有趣的事，不是吗？

sentences.en: One of them is that he says, you are being denied the wine at mass.
sentences.zh: 其中之一是他说，你们在弥撒中被剥夺了饮用葡萄酒的权力。

sentences.en: You should have both bread and wine.
sentences.zh: 你们本应既有面包又有酒。

sentences.en: And basically the priests are hogging all the wine for themselves.
sentences.zh: 基本上是神父们把所有的酒都据为己有。

sentences.en: But everyone should have it.
sentences.zh: 但每个人都应该享用它。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And because this is, you know, it's not just a little glass of wine.
sentences.zh: 因为这，你知道的，这不仅仅是一小杯酒。

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: This is the blood of Christ sharing in the radiant power of God.
sentences.zh: 这是基督的血，分享着上帝那夺目光辉的力量。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 确实。

sentences.en: And the second thing is that there's a linguistic nationalism to Hus, isn't there?
sentences.zh: 第二件事是，胡斯身上有一种语言民族主义，对吧？

sentences.en: So he wants lots of stuff to be in the Czech language, a bit like Wycliffe with the English language, and that that will play a part in the later Reformation.
sentences.zh: 所以他希望很多东西都用捷克语呈现，有点像威克里夫用英语一样，这在后来的宗教改革中发挥了一定作用。

sentences.en: Well, that's more complicated because actually, so Wycliffe translates the Bible into English,
sentences.zh: 嗯，情况要复杂得多，因为实际上，威克里夫把圣经翻译成了英语，

sentences.en: but it's condemned not because he's translated it into English, but because it's associated with him and his heretical followers.
sentences.zh: 但它受到谴责并不是因为他把它翻译成了英语，而是因为它与他和他的异端追随者联系在一起。

sentences.en: So it's over the course of the 15th century that an association on the part of the church authorities is starting to develop with heresy and with the Bible in vernacular languages,
sentences.zh: 所以在15世纪的进程中，教会权威开始将异端与使用地方语言（而非拉丁语）的圣经联系起来。

sentences.en: so not in Latin.
sentences.zh: 也就是不用拉丁语。

sentences.en: But it's not been absolutely solidified at this point.
sentences.zh: 但在当时，这种联系还没有彻底稳固。

sentences.en: But there's a hint of it, right?
sentences.zh: 但已经有了这种苗头，对吧？

sentences.en: Yeah, there is a hint.
sentences.zh: 是的，确实有这个苗头。

sentences.en: It really only gets kind of bedded down in the 16th century as a reaction to the Reformation.
sentences.zh: 直到16世纪，作为对宗教改革的反弹，这种联系才真正扎根稳固。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: But yeah, that is a part of it as well.
sentences.zh: 不过是的，这也是其中的一部分。

sentences.en: So Hus is seen as a troublemaker.
sentences.zh: 所以胡斯被视为一个麻烦制造者。

sentences.en: He gets invited to a church council in 1414 that is being held in the Swiss city of Constance,
sentences.zh: 他被邀请参加1414年在瑞士城市康斯坦茨召开的宗教会议，

sentences.en: and he is given a safe conduct there by the imperial authorities, by the guy who will go on to become the emperor.
sentences.zh: 他在那里得到了帝国当局（即日后将成为皇帝的那个人）颁发的安全通行证。

sentences.en: So he arrives there in November 1414.
sentences.zh: 于是他在1414年11月抵达那里。

sentences.en: Three weeks later, he is arrested.
sentences.zh: 三周后，他被捕了。

sentences.en: He's put on trial.
sentences.zh: 他被送上法庭受审。

sentences.en: He's told to recant.
sentences.zh: 他被要求认罪悔改。

sentences.en: He doesn't.
sentences.zh: 他拒绝了。

sentences.en: He's burnt at the stake, and his ashes are dumped in the Rhine.
sentences.zh: 他在火刑柱上被烧死，骨灰被倾倒在莱茵河里。

sentences.en: Oh, that's harsh.
sentences.zh: 哦，这也太残酷了。

sentences.en: And so that, I mean, that's a kind of a chilling example of what can happen if you push the church too far.
sentences.zh: 所以，我的意思是，这是一个令人不寒而栗的例子，展示了如果你把教会逼得太紧会发生什么。

sentences.en: But I think it is important to emphasize that not everyone who says that the church is corrupt or that it needs reform or that improvements can be made is seen as a heretic.
sentences.zh: 但我认为必须强调的是，并不是每一个说教会腐败、需要改革或可以改进的人都被视为异端。

sentences.en: This is something that is part of the fabric of the traditions of the medieval church.
sentences.zh: 这是中世纪教会传统结构的一部分。

sentences.en: So you can go too far and end up burnt.
sentences.zh: 所以你可能会做得过头，最终被烧死。

sentences.en: But equally, you can make these arguments and absolutely stay within the fabric of the church.
sentences.zh: 但同样地，你也可以提出这些论点，并且完全停留在教会的体制之内。

sentences.en: And doesn't that reflect the fact that the church is not static, that Christianity is not
sentences.zh: 这难道不反映了这样一个事实：教会并非一成不变的，基督教也不是一个固定不变的事物，

sentences.en: a fixed thing, and that there are always arguments going on like, should the pope have power or should it be councils of clergymen?
sentences.zh: 而且总是有各种争论在进行，比如：教皇应该拥有权力，还是应该由神职人员会议来掌权？

sentences.en: What is the exact relationship between church and state, as it were?
sentences.zh: 可以说，教会与国家之间的确切关系是什么？

sentences.en: So the pope's always falling out with secular rulers, isn't he?
sentences.zh: 所以教皇总是与世俗统治者闹翻，不是吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, this is constantly being negotiated.
sentences.zh: 是的，这一直在不断协商中。

sentences.en: So just to go back to the thing that we began this with.
sentences.zh: 所以回到我们最初的话题。

sentences.en: So indulgences.
sentences.zh: 也就是赎罪券。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: I mean, this is what Chaucer's pardoner is selling, the most loathsome figure in the
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是乔叟笔下的赦罪者在贩卖的东西，也就是我们在节目中讨论过的《坎特伯雷故事集》中最令人厌恶的人物。

sentences.en: Canterbury Tales we talked about in our episode.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，他太糟糕了。

sentences.en: I mean, he's terrible.
sentences.zh: 但乔叟并没有被斥为异端。

sentences.en: But Chaucer is not condemned as a heretic.
sentences.zh: 他最终被安葬在威斯敏斯特教堂。

sentences.en: He ends up buried in Westminster Abbey.
sentences.zh: 如果你愿意的话，你可以批评这种精神经济的各个方面。

sentences.en: You can criticize aspects of this spiritual economy, if you want to call it that.
sentences.zh: 并且依然可以是一个极其虔诚的天主教徒。

sentences.en: And be a completely devout Catholic Christian.
sentences.zh: 所以我认为，正是在这个意义上，宗教改革并不是不可避免的，你可以批评教会，但不必把整个体制都推倒。

sentences.en: So I think it's in that sense that there is nothing inevitable about the Reformation, that you can criticize the church, but you don't have to kind of pull the whole fabric down.
sentences.zh: 所以问题又来了，为什么它偏偏在1517年爆发，也就是我们这期节目一开始提到的那场关于赎罪券的争端？

sentences.en: And so again, the question is, why does it end up kicking off in 1517, this kind of, you know, indulgences bust up that we began this episode with?
sentences.zh: 同样地，为什么它偏偏由我们刚才提到的小伙子引发？

sentences.en: And equally, why does it end up kicking off with this guy who we left?
sentences.zh: 你知道的，他当时刚从大学毕业。

sentences.en: You know, he's just graduated from university.
sentences.zh: 他的父亲希望他去当一名律师。

sentences.en: His father wants him to go and be a lawyer.
sentences.zh: 他身上没有任何迹象表明他会引发拉丁欧洲基督徒自我认知方式上的这种全球性重大变革。

sentences.en: There's nothing about him that suggests he's going to precipitate this globally significant transformation in the way that Christians in Latin Europe think about themselves.
sentences.zh: 你知道，究竟发生了什么？

sentences.en: You know, what is it that happens?
sentences.zh: 好吧。

sentences.en: All right.
sentences.zh: 汤姆，这本该是这期节目最初的大约十分钟内容，但它却变成了整期节目，

sentences.en: Well, Tom, this was meant to be like the first 10 minutes or so of the episode, but it's
sentences.zh: 这太棒了，因为我觉得这是一个内容极其丰富且有趣的主题。

sentences.en: become the whole episode, which is great because I find it such a rich and interesting subject.
sentences.zh: 所以对于我们这个小教派“历史其余部分俱乐部”的各位会员来说，

sentences.en: So for those of you who are members of our very own little sect, the Rest is History Club,
sentences.zh: 你们当然可以立刻收听节目的其余部分。

sentences.en: you can, of course, hear the rest of the episodes right now.
sentences.zh: 所以你们可以去了解是什么让路德站到了教会的对立面，以及所有那些疯狂的事情。

sentences.en: So you can find out what turned Luther against the church, all the crazy stuff that happened.
sentences.zh: 接下来还有很多惊心动魄的内容。

sentences.en: There's lots of sort of blood and thunder to come.
sentences.zh: 所以你们可以马上深入了解。

sentences.en: So you can dig into that right away.
sentences.zh: 对于那些依然忠于老方法、每隔一段时间等新节目一发布就收听的听众朋友们，这很好。

sentences.en: For those of you who are still loyal to the old ways of listening to an episode every, you know, when it comes out, that's great.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们也喜欢你们。

sentences.en: You know, we like you too.
sentences.zh: 我们不会谴责你们。

sentences.en: We don't condemn you.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
